I politely disagree. Mirror's Edge fundamentally was built around moving through certain areas as fast as your various athletic tricks would allow you too, especially with vertical movement in confined spaces. It really boils down to optimizing your moves, which is why the game also is quite popular in the speedrunning community.

Randomly slapping an open world system onto it for no apparent reason (rather than making more numerous and/or varied levels) defeats this entire purpose because you constantly have to jog from mission to mission before you get to the actual speed segments. A sandbox, by design, can never have the same quality as enclosed levels, which allow the designers to carefully consider the location of every single object.
